subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards gain an explicit non-full-content escape hatch for long replies, keep only coalesced full-content updates, or preserve full-content-only behavior and document the latency tradeoff?
rationale: Current main preserves full-content updates for truncation safety, but live reports show severe latency and the linked coalescing PR appears insufficient; the default behavior and any new config/mode need maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor an opt-in escape hatch
options.body: Keep full-content CardKit updates as the default and add a documented opt-in append, segment, or equivalent mode with live proof that it improves long-reply latency without truncating content.

options.title: Continue with coalescing only
options.body: Use the linked PR direction if maintainers believe fewer full-content updates are enough, but require exact-head live Feishu timing proof before treating this issue as fixed.

options.title: Document full-content-only tradeoff
options.body: Decline a new mode and document that streaming cards may be slow for long replies, with `streaming: false` or another existing delivery mode as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Sponsor an opt-in escape hatch
recommendation.body: Keep full-content CardKit updates as the default and add a documented opt-in append, segment, or equivalent mode with live proof that it improves long-reply latency without truncating content.

likelyOwner.reason: CONTRIBUTING.md lists this person for Feishu and related Chinese channels, making them the best available decision owner for the channel-level product/config tradeoff.
